title: Mysterious Are the Ways of God
description: Mysterious Are the Ways of God in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 631 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God Merciful in Affliction”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Mys-te-rious are the ways of God, And fear and blind-ness oft re-pine; We mur-mur 'neath his chas-tening rod, Be-cause we read not his de-sign.

lines: Mysterious are the ways of God,
And fear and blindness oft repine;
We murmur 'neath his chastening rod,
Because we read not his design.
Impending clouds his love has spread
O'er this low vale where mortals dwell;
And oft we mourn his spirit fled,
When adverse tempests round us swell.
But in those storms that sometimes roll,
Our mortal dwellings dark above,
Whose threatening shades dismay the soul,
Dwells the bright presence of his love.
We cannot see him — not a ray
Of all his glory there appears,
And oft we thread our darkened way,
Trembling with anxious doubts and fears.
Yet faith still looks beyond the gloom,
While hope's bright star illumes our night;
Pilgrims of earth! though dark the tomb,
It leads to scenes of bliss and light.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
